(3) issue the very next request with the identical token and assert the EXACT denial: 403, body {error: 'You no longer have access to this organization', code: 'ORG_MEMBERSHIP_REVOKED'} — this is the literal output of the deny() helper in auditsStrictMembership.middleware.ts, which requireActiveAuditsMembership uses on every non-ACTIVE status with no caching (the module re-reads organization_members on every single request by design, per its own header comment). (4) prove zero fallback: no business payload in the denial response body, a direct count of the underlying table shows no new/mutated row, and the membership table itself is read fresh (not from a 60s cache, unlike the general-purpose validateOrgMembership this guard deliberately does not use). (5) state the vacuity check: if requireActiveAuditsMembership were removed from the Gateway.ts mount, step 3's request would reach the router with only gatewayVerifyToken's identity attachment in front of it, which does not consult organization_members at all for this path — so the exact-same request would return 200 with business data instead of 403, proving the control is load-bearing.

AND organization_id = ?` on every single request with no cache layer — this is called out explicitly in the module's own header comment as the deliberate difference from the general-purpose validateOrgMembership (60s cache, fail-open on DB error). wireDiscoveredButNotYetRun.mountPoint: Gateway.ts:1331 — app.use('/api/audits', gatewayVerifyToken, auditsStrictMembership, auditsMethodRouter) — this is the real production mount this gate must drive a supertest request through, not a hand-rolled Express app that re-attaches the same middleware functions in a different wiring.
wireDiscoveredButNotYetRun.orgFallbackWrinkle: auth.middleware.ts's attachUser has a deliberate rescue: if the token's resolved organization is NOT an ACTIVE membership for the user, it searches for ANY OTHER ACTIVE org for that user and silently switches req.organizationId to it (comment-labeled 'BUG-02/15' rescue). This means the test fixture MUST give the token-holder exactly ONE organization_members row (the one that gets revoked) — if the user had a second ACTIVE membership elsewhere, step 3 would silently switch tenants and pass instead of deny, which would be a false negative for this exact gate. This wrinkle is the reason a naively-written version of this test could pass for the wrong reason, and is being recorded here before the test is written so the fixture design is auditable independent of the result.
wireDiscoveredButNotYetRun.jtiOmission: The signed test token must omit the jti claim (or use one not present in revoked_tokens) — checkTokenRevocation short-circuits to attachUser immediately when no jti is present, keeping the token-revocation check (a different, unrelated mechanism) out of this test's causal path.
